title: Shapes of SOCl2, XeOF4, ClF3, ClF5, XeF5+, SO3 2-, XeF3+ and SF4 by VSEPR: see-saw, T-shaped, trigonal planar and square pyramidal counts
summary: Eight species on eight cards. For each, the lab counts the valence electrons on the central atom, subtracts those used in bonds and the charge, and finds the lone pairs and steric number. The electron domains are then relaxed on a sphere by mutual repulsion - first all alike into the ideal polyhedron, then with lone pairs pushing harder, every placement tried and the lowest energy kept - and each rotating 3-D model is named from the angles between its bonded atoms. The species drop into shape bins, the counts are matched to List-II and options A-D are tested. No prediction stage - input, run, watch, result.
subject: Chemistry
topic: VSEPR theory - lone pairs, steric number and molecular shapes of main-group and xenon species
subtopics: Counting lone pairs on the central atom
Shapes with lone pairs: see-saw, T-shaped, square pyramidal, trigonal pyramidal
concepts: Lone pairs = (valence electrons - electrons used in bonds - charge)/2; F and Cl use 1 electron, O uses 2
ClF3 and XeF3+: SN 5, 2 LP equatorial - T-shaped
XeOF4, ClF5 and XeF5+: SN 6, 1 LP - square pyramidal
SOCl2 and SO3 2-: SN 4, 1 LP - trigonal pyramidal, so no species is trigonal planar
Counts 1, 2, 0, 3 give P1 Q2 R5 S3 - option A

derivedQuantities.lone_pairs: SOCl2 1, XeOF4 1, ClF3 2, ClF5 1, XeF5+ 1, SO3 2- 1, XeF3+ 2, SF4 1

methods: Solved independently before any key was consulted: see-saw 1, T-shaped 2, trigonal planar 0, square pyramidal 3 - option A
Lone pairs counted two ways (central-atom rule and a full Lewis-structure electron count) - they agree for all eight species
A separate repulsion model (1/r^8, its own lone-pair weights, scipy from 40 random starts) gives the same eight shapes as the AXnEm table and as the page
Controls: SO3 trigonal planar, XeF4 square planar, SF6 octahedral
Independent script tests/verify_p1q14.py: 30 of 30 checks pass
Solution websites: MathonGo's published solution (their Q46) gives A
The page counts electrons, relaxes the domains (every lone-pair placement tried) and names each shape from its bond angles at run time; no shape or answer is written into the script

Headless-browser suite tests/sim_p1q14.js drives the whole page: the engine and its controls, the answer above the experiment and the dock below it, conditions and warnings, the automatic eight-stage run, the gauges walking through the species, tiles, board, badges, charts, the reveal, the VSEPR builder, replay, pause, reset, a custom run, classroom mode, 390 and 360 px, reduced motion, the feed entries and the real app shell opening it
Answer cross-checked afterwards against the official final key printed with the Paper 1 PDF: Q14 -> A
verification.note: The repulsion model reproduces the shapes and the direction of lone-pair compression (angles below 90° and 109.5°); it is not meant to give exact experimental angles.
